pageCache.pageTitle: Deerhurst and Apperley CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Deerhurst and Apperley Church of England Primary School is a Voluntary Controlled, co-educational school, situated in the charming village of Apperley in Gloucestershire.
We welcome just under 100 learners into our school and are committed to knowing every individual, to help them to be the very best version of themselves. Each of our classes is led by enthusiastic and experienced teachers and supported by dedicated teaching assistants. Our pupils are valued, nurtured, and encouraged to grow academically, socially, and spiritually, with excellent pastoral care at the heart of everything we do.
Our school buildings are welcoming, well-resourced, and designed to support learning in a variety of ways. Outdoor areas and classrooms provide stimulating environments for every learner.
While the school’s Christian ethos is strong and well-supported by the local church, we also welcome children with other faiths or no faith. We are proud of the strong relationships we hold with our families and wider school community, ensuring that children feel well supported and valued.
Quick Links

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision & Values — Deerhurst and Apperley CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
More news to follow as we develop our vision together with our school community
Working together with our whole school community, we have identified six core values that provide a shared foundation and a common understanding for everyone in our school. Rooted in our Christian vision and inspired by the teachings of God, these values help us to understand how we can live, learn and grow together.
Our core values are woven through every aspect of school life. They shape our learning in collective worship, encourage us to reflect on our actions and relationships, and guide the way we treat one another with care, respect and compassion. They also inspire us as we develop our school community, embrace new opportunities and strive to be the very best versions of ourselves.
By living out these values each day, we nurture a school environment where every member of our community is valued, supported and encouraged to flourish.
Hand in hand, our core school values walk alongside the five fundamental British Values. Through collective worship, Religious Education (RE), Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE), and across our wider curriculum, we make meaningful connections between these values and our daily lives. By exploring these links, pupils deepen their understanding of themselves, their responsibilities to others, and their place within the wider world.
Our learning encourages children to appreciate diversity, show respect, make informed choices, and contribute positively to their communities. Grounded in our Christian vision, this approach helps pupils develop as thoughtful, compassionate and responsible citizens who are well prepared for life.
Our approach to spiritual, moral, social and cultural development is designed to help children look beyond themselves and recognise the difference they can make in the world around them. Rooted in our Christian vision, we nurture curiosity, compassion, responsibility and hope, helping children to see the world as a place full of opportunity, purpose and possibility.
Through our behaviour and homework systems, we intentionally signpost and celebrate those moments when children connect with others, care for their environment and contribute positively to their community. In this way, they develop a growing sense of advocacy and purpose through their interactions with family, friends and the wider community.
The opportunities available to our children are limited only by their imagination and creativity. They have donated their own books to furnish the community library, taken part in village litter picks, cooked for their families, completed simple DIY projects and established a school newspaper. These meaningful experiences help children understand that their actions matter and that they can be a force for good.
Across our curriculum, collective worship and wider school life, children explore big questions, reflect on their beliefs and values, and learn to respect the views of others. By encouraging them to use their gifts in service of others, we help them develop the confidence to contribute to the flourishing of their community and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: PE & Sports Premium — Deerhurst and Apperley CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
PE & Sport Premium
The Primary PE & Sport Premium is given to improve the provision of physical education (PE) and sport in primary schools in England.
Vision: All pupils leaving primary school physically literate and with the knowledge, skills and motivation necessary to equip them for a healthy lifestyle and lifelong participation in physical activity and sport.
Objective: To achieve self-sustaining improvement in the quality of PE and sport in primary schools through:
The engagement of all pupils in regular physical activity – kick-starting healthy active lifestyles.
The profile of PE and sport being raised across the school as a tool for whole school improvement.
Increased confidence, knowledge and skills of all staff in teaching PE and sport.
Broader experience of a range of sports and activities offered to all pupils.
Increased participation in competitive sport.

pageCache.pageTitle: Clubs — Deerhurst and Apperley CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
After School Clubs
At our small primary school, we are proud to offer a wide range of extra-curricular clubs designed to inspire, engage and enrich our pupils' learning beyond the classroom.
Each half-term, we provide a fresh selection of clubs run by both our talented class teachers and visiting specialists. These clubs reflect the interests and strengths of our staff and community, and may include:
Sports Clubs – from football and multisports to scooting and table tennis
Camp Kindness – have fun together with craft activities
Drama & Performance Club – build confidence and have fun with role-play and storytelling
Our club offerings change regularly to keep things fresh and exciting, and to give children the opportunity to try something new each term.
For details about the clubs available this half-term, please contact the school office directly.

pageCache.pageTitle: Introduction — Deerhurst and Apperley CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Introduction to the Curriculum
The Deerhurst Drivers underpin our curriculum vision and our unwavering commitment to every learner. They ensure that our curriculum is ambitious, inclusive and coherently sequenced, rather than simply delivered. Through a carefully curated approach, we promote equity of opportunity, nurture aspiration and secure strong outcomes, while remaining responsive to the diverse needs, experiences and potential of the learners in front of us.
At Deerhurst and Apperley School, our curriculum is designed to give every child the knowledge, skills, and confidence they need to thrive, both now and in the future. We are committed to providing a rich, ambitious education that is accessible to all learners, and we shape our curriculum through the lens of every child who walks through our doors. This means recognising and building on the cultural capital our pupils already bring, while thoughtfully adapting our teaching to expand the horizons of all of our learners.
Our approach is rooted in clear intent, purposeful implementation, and meaningful impact. Staff work collaboratively to plan and refine learning sequences that are coherent, well‑structured, and responsive to each cohort. Through ongoing reflection, assessment, and professional dialogue, we ensure that how we teach it, continually evolves in response to our learners so that all learners can achieve the high aspirations we hold for them.
We believe that learning is a shared journey. By working closely with our pupils, listening to their experiences, and understanding their starting points, we make adaptations to ensure our curriculum that is both inclusive and aspirational. Our aim is simple: to give every child the best possible foundation for the next stage of their education and for life beyond primary school.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND — Deerhurst and Apperley CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
At our school, we are deeply committed to supporting pupils with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) through early identification, thoughtful intervention, and ongoing monitoring of progress. We work closely with families, teachers, and external professionals to build a clear understanding of each child’s strengths and needs, ensuring that support is tailored and effective.
Our inclusive approach means that learning is adapted so every child can access the curriculum, participate fully in school life, and flourish both academically and personally. Guided by the SEND Code of Practice, we strive to create an environment where every pupil feels valued, supported, and empowered to achieve their very best.
Our SEND co-ordinator is Mrs Phillcox and she is happy to chat though any concerns you may have about a child's progress. In collaborative discussions with parents, carers, teachers and the SENCO we may feel that your child has need for support or help from an external agency such as Speech and Language Therapy, Learning Support or Educational Psychologists.
For pupils at Deerhurst & Apperley CE Primary School, their needs are met using three levels of intervention, described as ‘waves of support’ which support access to the new National Curriculum.
Wave 1 is the provision of quality inclusive teaching which takes into account the learning needs of all the pupils in the classroom. It includes differentiated work, flexible groups and creating an inclusive learning environment.
Wave 2 is the provision of specific, additional time limited interventions provided for some pupils who need help to accelerate their progress or enable them to work at or above their age-related expectations. They are often targeted at a group of pupils with similar needs.
Wave 3 is the targeted provision for a minority of pupils where it is necessary to provide highly tailored intervention to accelerate progress or enable children to achieve their potential.
We also follow the SEND Assess, Plan, Do, Review Cycle as recommended in the SEND Code of Practice 2014, to inform the support we offer children with additional needs.
As part of the 'Children's and Families Act 2014' every provider for additional needs is required to give a summary of what it can offer to help support and care for pupils that may require additional support in school. This is known as the 'SEND Information Report'.
Please click and download the link below for details of what we offer as a school and further details about who best to contact if you have any further queries or questions.

pageCache.pageTitle: EYFS/Reception — Deerhurst and Apperley CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Early Years Foundation Stage (Reception)
Deerhurst & Apperley CE Primary School warmly welcomes children who are aged 3 in Little Deers Preschool and 4 (for Reception) before the 31st August. The Reception year is very exciting for our youngest children and we look forward to working in partnership with their families to help them settle in and enjoy school and learning.
We like our children to:
be happy, independent risk takers
be confident, resilient and persevere with their learning
be excited, motivated and love to learn
thrive emotionally, physically, academically and creatively
develop a growth mindset to help them problem-solve and face new challenges
We believe that children learn best through practical, hands-on experiences and interactions with their environment and that play underpins the delivery of the EYFS. The best outcomes for children’s learning occur when most of the activities within a child’s day are a mixture of:
Child-initiated play, actively supported by adults
Focused learning — with adults guiding their learning through rich experiential activities
Child initiated time provides children with opportunities to consolidate and extend their skills and the concepts learnt.
Learning and development
There are seven areas of learning and development that shape the educational provision in early years settings.
All areas of learning and development are important and inter-connected. The three prime areas are particularly crucial for building capacity to learn, form relationships and thrive.
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Communication and Language
Physical Development
Understanding the world
Expressive arts and design
Within any group of 3 and 5-year-olds there will be a huge variation in development. For this reason, it is vital that we meet individual needs and that the activities provided for each child will be tailored with the aim of meeting their individual needs.
Characteristics of Effective Teaching and Learning
The characteristics of effective teaching and learning underpin achievement of the prime and specific areas of learning. They represent processes rather than outcomes and allow us to understand how a child learns.
The characteristics are:
Playing and Exploring - Children investigate and experience things, and ‘have a go’.
Active Learning - Children concentrate and keep on trying if they encounter difficulties, and enjoy achievements.
Creating and Thinking Critically - Children have and develop their own ideas, make links between ideas, and develop strategies for doing things.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pupil Premium — Deerhurst and Apperley CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium
How we use the Pupil Premium?
Pupil Premium is additional funding provided by the government to help schools reduce the barriers disadvantaged pupils may face in accessing education. Rather than being allocated as an individual pot of money for each eligible child, the funding is used to develop a whole‑school strategy that supports positive outcomes for all. At our school, we use Pupil Premium to enhance teaching, provide targeted support, and widen opportunities, ensuring every child, regardless of background, can thrive and achieve their full potential.
Pupil Premium money is sent to schools for the support of students who match any of the following criteria.
· They are in receipt of Free School Meals (FSM)
· They have been in receipt of FSM at some point in the last six year
· Children from families connected with the Armed Forces
· Children who are adopted and were previously in care
From January 2026, Gloucestershire County Council (GCC) will introduce an opt-out auto-award approach to Free School Meals (FSM). This approach helps to make sure that children in Gloucestershire who are entitled to FSM do not miss out on receiving them. The scheme will also support schools with additional funding opportunities.
How will the impact of this spending be measured?
We track the progress of all pupils on a regular basis (both day-to-day and termly). Every term, teachers, governors and the headteacher meet to discuss pupil progress in order to ensure all the pupils needs are met and to make plans to help children that may need additional support in a particular area of the curriculum. Other information based upon pastoral indicators will also be discussed on a regular basis to ensure all pupils' needs can be met with the support of this additional funding.
Please contact us if you should wish to further discuss what we are doing to support learners across the school community.
What do we get and what impact does it have?
View our Annual Strategy Report on the money we receive for Pupil Premium and the impact this has upon the outcomes for our disadvantaged pupils.

pageCache.pageTitle: Governors — Deerhurst and Apperley CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Governors
The governing body plays a vital role in supporting and shaping the future of the school. Working closely with school leaders, governors help to ensure that the school's vision, ethos and strategic direction remain clear, ambitious and firmly focused on providing the very best outcomes for all pupils. Through their commitment and dedication, they help maintain the values that underpin school life while supporting leaders in delivering a high-quality education.
Governors provide both support and constructive challenge, helping to ensure that the Headteacher is empowered to lead the school effectively and that educational standards continue to develop and improve. They take a keen interest in teaching, learning and pupil outcomes, celebrating successes while working collaboratively with staff to address priorities for development.
A further key responsibility of the governing body is overseeing the effective use of the school's financial resources. By ensuring that funding is managed carefully and strategically, governors help secure the resources, staffing and learning opportunities that enable pupils and staff to flourish.
To carry out their responsibilities effectively, the governing body operates through three committees: Ethos & Personnel, Finance & Premises, and Standards & Curriculum in addition to full governing board meetings. Governors contribute their time, expertise and experience across these areas, bringing a wealth of knowledge and a shared commitment to the success of the school.
An active and engaged governing body is one of the school's greatest strengths. Through regular visits, meetings and involvement in school life, governors develop a strong understanding of the community they serve. Their support for staff, commitment to continuous improvement and unwavering focus on pupils help create a positive partnership that benefits the entire school community and contributes significantly to the school's ongoing success.
